why: A customer at home taps order on a phone; 'arrives tomorrow' shows, then a wall calendar flips from Tuesday to Thursday while her doorstep stays empty.
Her message lands on a colleague's screen at an office desk; the colleague looks up at a dim miniature world of stations they cannot yet read.
The camera pulls back over the whole isometric world: order office, warehouse, hub, depot and the customer's street joined by one road; a token passes from station to station.
The five stations light up one by one along the road as each is named, each with a small label that stays as a quiet map key.
Close on the order station: the lamp's order card arrives, a payment check ticks, and the amount shows as held, not yet taken.
Two more checks pass over the lamp's order card and it moves on; a ghost order beside it is flagged and drops into a held tray.
A lamp in the stock records is tagged with the order, and the order card travels along the road into the warehouse, joining a pick queue.
A cut-off line across the order station's clock; an order before it joins today's batch, an order after it slides into the next batch.
The website says 'In stock' while the warehouse shelf it points to stands empty; the mismatch is marked.
Inside the isometric warehouse a picker's handheld shows an aisle and shelf; the picker walks the aisle and lifts the lamp box; the word appears only at the end.
At a packing bench the lamp is scanned, boxed, sealed, and a label prints and goes on; from here the labelled box is the lamp's look for the rest of the film.
Three small trouble spots appear in the warehouse in turn as named: a wrong box in a cart, an empty shelf slot, a long queue at packing.
The lamp's box rides a truck to a large hub where trucks from other directions also unload; inside, a scanner arch reads its label and a diverter sends it down the lane for her region.
Night falls; outbound trucks wait at the hub's doors under a departure board, and the first one pulls out on time.
The lamp's box reaches the dock just as its truck's doors close; the truck leaves and the box sits alone under the board showing the next departure.
On the sorter a ghost box with a torn label is kicked to a side lane and another rides the wrong lane.
At the depot near her street, boxes go into a van in stop order while a route line draws itself across the neighbourhood.
The van stops at a house; the driver records proof on a handheld, showing signature, photo and scan as each is said.
Along the route four small troubles appear as named: a closed door, a house number that does not match, a van with no room, rain over the road.
The lamp's journey as a dotted road with no moving dot; a scan mark pops only at each station, and each pop adds its status line to a phone trail.
The lamp's own trail on the phone stops at 'At hub' with an empty gap below; the world behind is dimmed so the viewer has to choose.
The world lights again with the hub highlighted; the lamp's box sits on the dock with the two likely causes marked beside it.
Back at the colleague's desk, three short steps build beside the message thread as the colleague types a reply.
The customer reads the reply at home; the camera rises over the world as a truck pulls away from the hub with the lamp's box toward her street, the pocket rule over the sky.
